safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports no previous similar episodes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states no prior similar episodes; generated facts do not address prior similar reactions/episodes.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the patient has had no prior similar episodes can reduce clarity around whether this is a first-time systemic reaction versus a recurrent pattern, which may influence documentation and risk counseling. However, it is unlikely to change the immediate management in this case where emergent evaluation is already advised.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold assessment includes possible urticaria/hives; generated assessment does not mention urticaria/hives.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to mention possible urticaria/hives omits a supportive feature of an allergic reaction and may reduce diagnostic completeness. It is unlikely to materially change urgent disposition (ambulance/ED) already recommended for breathing symptoms.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither gold nor transcript documents denial of wheeze; wheeze is not discussed in the encounter.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting a denial of wheeze when it was not assessed/elicited can mislead clinicians into discounting bronchospasm/asthma involvement in an allergic reaction. This could contribute to incomplete reassessment or delayed escalation if later clinicians rely on the note rather than re-evaluating.

safety_verdicts.content: Suspected anaphylaxis secondary to wasp sting
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold/transcript indicate concern to rule out anaphylaxis ('in case you develop an anaphylactic reaction'), not that anaphylaxis is already suspected/diagnosed. The generated statement increases certainty beyond what is supported.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating 'suspected anaphylaxis' increases diagnostic certainty beyond the transcript’s more cautious 'in case you develop an anaphylactic reaction.' Overstating severity could prompt unnecessary interventions (e.g., early epinephrine or higher-acuity labeling) but is less likely to cause direct harm than missing anaphylaxis.

While shallow breathing and chest tightness are correctly captured, the unsupported wheeze denial can still lead to mild downstream clinical miscommunication.
